text:
maya: quick heads-up — after flipping the gateway to NLB (tls passthrough) we started seeing intermittent 503s for inference-gateway. happens during scale-up and also sporadically under steady load. anyone seen this pattern?

jordan: do you have the service & targetGroup config? most likely healthcheck mismatch or externalTrafficPolicy.

maya: here's the service we applied (k8s svc type: LoadBalancer, target-type ip):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: ip
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
  ports:
    - name: tls
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
```

lee: with target-type=ip and externalTrafficPolicy=Local the NLB will healthcheck the pod IPs directly. if the probe port / protocol is wrong you'll see nodes removed from target group and 503s. what are the healthcheck settings on the TG?

maya: TG health check is TCP on port 8443, interval 10s, healthy threshold 3. logs show a handful of FailedHealthChecks around scale events.

sam: two quick things to double-check: 1) kube-proxy iptables ipvs mode can drop traffic during pod lifecycle, 2) make sure the pod readinessProbe actually responds on the same port/protocol the NLB checks. if readinessProbe is HTTP but TG is TCP you'll get a mismatch.

jordan: also check subnets: targetType=ip requires ENI/pod networking to be stable. if pods get restarted on different nodes during scale, TG target registration latency can cause transient failures. 

maya: good call — readinessProbe is HTTP GET /healthz on 8080, but container serves TLS on 8443 and we had a sidecar proxy routing from 8443->8080 for the app. so NLB TCP healthcheck to 8443 won't hit the HTTP endpoint.

lee: yep that's the culprit. options: change TG healthcheck to HTTP on 8443 (if TLS termination), or make NLB do TCP to the exact port that responds with raw TCP success, or switch externalTrafficPolicy to Cluster and use node-level healthchecks depending on target-type.

sam: if you want TLS passthrough, TG must do TCP and the endpoint must accept a raw TCP handshake. If you want HTTP healthchecks, you need TLS termination at the LB (alb or NLB with TLS termination) or use a sidecar that answers TCP-level healthchecks.

maya: thinking to try the smallest change first: set service.externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster so node-level checks pass and see if outages stop. i'll also add a readinessProbe on 8443 that does a TCP check.

jordan: SGTM. also add these annotations to the TG / terraform if you change target_type or healthcheck: 
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "inference" {
  name     = "tg-inference"
  port     = 8443
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    enabled             = true
    protocol            = "TCP"
    port                = "8443"
    interval            = 10
    healthy_threshold   = 3
    unhealthy_threshold = 3
  }
}
```

ops-bot: deploy-check: infra/1721 -> plan looks safe; changing externalTrafficPolicy to Cluster on service/inference-gateway and adding tcp readinessProbe on port 8443. no new IAM or infra resources. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks all — i'll open PR with the svc tweak + readinessProbe change and run canary on staging. will update here after the canary. :pray:
